$comment: These are the tasks that answer 'can a model use this toolset at all', one per
capability area, and they are what `npm run bench` runs by default. They are
also the tasks whose failure modes are the least ambiguous: a wrong answer here
means the model did not reach for a tool it needed.
Every expected value was produced by running the shipped tool (see
benchmark/_probe.mjs and _probe-all.mjs), never typed from memory. `covers`
names the tools the task exercises; benchmark/verifications.mjs carries the
inputs that reproduce the `where: "tool"` expectations, and
test/benchmark-coverage.mjs fails if any registered tool is missing from every

tasks.instruction: I have this DNA oligo: ATGCGTACGTTAGCCTAGGCAT. I need to order the reverse-complement strand. Give me the reverse-complement sequence and tell me the GC content of the original oligo.

assertions.note: reverse complement of the 22 nt input
GC percent of the original
GC percent restated in prose

tasks.instruction: There is a pUC118.dna file in your working directory. I want to linearise the whole plasmid with a single restriction digest — one cut, nothing else. Which enzymes can do that, and can you confirm one of them with its exact cut position?

assertions.note: pUC118 has 33 unique cutters in the catalogue
EcoRI cuts once, at position 927

tasks.instruction: My digest of pUC118.dna (working directory) with BamHI is barely working — almost no cut, even though the site is definitely in the sequence. Someone suggested Dam methylation. Work out what is going on: check the plasmid's Dam and Dcm sites, and tell me what the methylation analysis says about BamHI and which enzymes the tool considers usable on this plasmid.

assertions.note: the tool flags BamHI

the methylation verdict must be reported. NOTE what is deliberately NOT asserted: there is no assertion that the model AGREES with the tool. Measured behaviour is that it runs molbio_methylation_check, then cross-checks NEB over the web, finds the plugin's quick-reference table disagrees (the table marks BamHI impaired by dam; NEB lists BamHI as dam-insensitive), and reports the disagreement. That is the right thing to do with a hand-transcribed table, so this task grades whether the model CONSULTED the analysis; the table discrepancy is logged in benchmark/README.md as a plugin-data question instead of being scored as a model failure.

tasks.instruction: Here are my qPCR Ct values from a knockdown experiment. Target gene: treated 22.1, 22.3, 22.0; control 25.0, 25.2, 24.9. Reference gene: treated 18.0, 18.1, 18.0; control 18.2, 18.1, 18.3. What is the fold change in the target gene in the treated samples relative to control, by the delta-delta Ct method?

assertions.note: fold change, rounded however the model likes

assertions.pattern: mismatch @seq1 (31|81) / seq2 (31|81): (A vs C|C vs A)
assertions.note: exactly one difference, at read position 31 and reference position 81. The assertion is deliberately AGNOSTIC about which argument is which: a model may pass `sequence1 = read`, and `molbio_align` reports identity symmetrically, so pinning `seq1 81 / seq2 31` graded an incidental argument order rather than the alignment. Both orders and both polarities are accepted; a missing or extra difference is not.

tasks.instruction:
Translate this DNA in frame 1 and find the open reading frames of at least 5 amino acids. Tell me the protein sequence and the length of the longest ORF in amino acids.

GGGATGGCTGCTGCTGCTGCTGCTGCTGCTGCTTAACCC

assertions.note: an ORF of the expected protein was found at all

the ORF's protein. The exact `A` count is not pinned to one digit: the tool reports `10 aa` for `MAAAAAAAAA` (ten residues) and a model that counts the nine residues before the stop codon writes `MAAAAAAAA` — both describe the same ORF, and which convention is 'right' is a genuine ambiguity the tool itself does not resolve (it renders `MAAAAAAAAA*P` for the frame and `10 aa` for the ORF).
the ORF length in either convention

tasks.instruction: Explain how BsaI and EcoRI differ: their recognition sites, how many bases away from the site they cut, and what kind of overhang each leaves.

assertions.pattern: BsaI: type IIS GGTCTC\(1/5\), cut 7/5, 4 bp 5' overhang

assertions.note: EcoRI's site, matched WITHOUT its leading G on purpose: the model legitimately writes the cut notation `G^AATTC` (and the spaced `G^A A T T C`), neither of which contains the contiguous literal `GAATTC`. Pinning that literal graded typography rather than the answer.
both enzymes leave a 4 nt overhang
the designer produced candidates at all

the tool's TOP-RANKED amplicon. NOTE what is not asserted: the direction the model reads the pair in. The tool prints `F` at 201-222 and `R` at 105-124 — F is DOWNSTREAM of R — and a model may legitimately report the opposite role assignment (or the reverse complement of a primer). The tool's own orientation inconsistency is a recorded plugin bug (benchmark/README.md Findings), not something this task should grade the model on.
one of the two molecules that make up the top-ranked pair, in either reading
the other one
an amplicon size inside the requested window

assertions.pattern: drops below Q30 from position 1 \(below Q20 from 11\)
assertions.note: the 3' collapse the user is worried about

the QC numbers, or at least the QC verdict, in prose. A model that exports the report as a deliverable and says 'the answers are in the attached report' has done the work but left the numbers out of the summary; that is a REPORTING observation, and it is recorded in benchmark/README.md rather than being the whole verdict — the tool assertions above already prove the analysis ran on the right data.

tasks.instruction:
Tell me about the GC composition of this 402 bp sequence: overall GC percent, and whether it contains any CpG island under the Gardiner-Garden criteria. If there is one, give me its coordinates, its length, and its own GC percent.

{seq:puc118_cpg_region}

assertions.note: overall GC of the fragment
the island's own GC, not the fragment's
overall GC stated in prose
island GC stated in prose — the two numbers must be told apart

tasks.instruction: I have a 10x stock and I need 1000 microlitres of a 0.5x working solution. How much of the stock do I need, and how much diluent?

assertions.note: the tool's own worked relation
50 volume units of stock
the remainder is diluent

tasks.instruction: No bioinformatics needed for this one, I just want to sanity-check my arithmetic: if I dilute 10 microlitres of a 50 mM solution into a final volume of 500 microlitres, what is the final concentration in mM?

assertions.note: 10 uL x 50 mM / 500 uL = 1 mM

tasks.instruction: Can you check my sequencing result for me?

assertions.note: the missing input must be asked for
the model must say it has nothing to work with rather than guess

a clarification, not a one-line refusal: at least 500 characters of substance. The first version demanded a literal `?`, which failed a perfectly clear bulleted request for the missing files — the headless composition has no question answerer, so the model is told to ask in prose and does so without question marks.
